correctness.rationale: Pairwise Frobenius-orthogonal cyclic shifts yield a unique circulant nearest point for every doubly stochastic input. The exact squared vertex-distance \(n-\sum_k m_k^2/n\) reduces the max to an integer minimum; modular displacement-sum obstruction excludes the all-one profile at even orders, and explicit permutations attain each sharp bound. A Hilbert-space variance identity and the fact that P-Q circulant forces both to be shifts if P,Q differ prove that no nonvertex farthest point exists. The second discrete level is bounded by the even parity of sum(m_k-1)^2 and achieved by explicit transpositions of construction permutations, with n=4 separately given. The bundled checker exhausts orders 2..8 and directly verifies \(3\le n\le1000\) constructions; 48 separate constrained optimization tests corroborate the projection formula. No finite test is used as the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The exact Frobenius nearest-circulant projection is acknowledged prior work, as is cyclic transversal existence/obstruction. The inspected sources on Birkhoff geometry, cyclic permutation polytopes and structured matrix approximation do not state the sharp Hausdorff value between the full Birkhoff polytope and its circulant subpolytope, identify all farthest points, or provide the sharp second vertex-distance level. The distance is not the known Chebyshev radius at a fixed center: the nearest point varies with the permutation, and the even-order correction is positive. An unindexed prior synthesis is a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: The full text of Goddyn-Halasz (2020) was not read; its abstract does not suggest a Frobenius Hausdorff theorem, but an older variant remains possible.

Older structured-matrix approximation and Latin transversal literature might contain a numerically equivalent extremal formula under alternative terminology; absence from indexed search is not proof of priority.
The pointwise projection and complete-mapping existence/obstruction are known, so only the full sharp geometric extremal classification plus first vertex-distance gap is proposed as the novel unit.

value.rationale: The inclusion of the cyclic-shift stochastic simplex in the full Birkhoff polytope is natural for translation-invariant Markov dynamics and permutation assignments. The exact Hausdorff loss, the parity obstruction, the full rigidity of worst inputs, and the sharp first discrete stability gap provide a complete infinite-family geometric invariant not supplied by the known pointwise projection. It is not an arbitrary numerical slice; the geometry is structurally tied to cyclic Latin transversals.
